about.metaDescription: What Cauce is, how it works and who made it.
about.hackathon: Project for the Mexican Space Agency (AEM) Hackathon
about.heroTitle: A live map of what floods Matamoros.
about.heroBody: Cauce brings together neighbors' reports, water-level sensor readings and the rain forecast in one place, so action happens before the next storm.
about.problemBody: On October 4, 2026, cold front No. 1 dropped 215.9 mm of rain on Matamoros. Neighborhoods like Buenavista, San Francisco and Los Sauces were cut off. Many floods start with something small: a drain clogged with trash that nobody reported in time.

report.title: Report
report.body: Take a photo, confirm the location and choose what's happening. It takes under 30 seconds, with no account.

confirm.title: Confirm
confirm.body: Neighbors say whether the problem is still there or fixed, so the map stays current without moderators.

measure.title: Measure
measure.body: Water-level sensors in drains and canals warn in real time when water rises.

anticipate.title: Anticipate
anticipate.body: With the rain forecast, history and satellite terrain data, authorities know which drains to clean first.

about.sensorsBody: We designed low-cost sensors (ESP32 with an ultrasonic sensor) that measure water height and send it every few minutes. Above the warning level, they report every minute.
about.authoritiesBody: The water utility (JAD) and Civil Protection get a dashboard with risk by area, the reasons behind each score, and the list of drains to clean before the rain.
about.privacyBody: We don't ask for an account or personal data. Photos are compressed on your phone and their metadata is removed before upload. Please avoid faces and license plates.
about.demoBody: For this presentation, the map includes reports and sensors simulated from real floods in Matamoros between 2024 and 2026. Illustrations are labeled.

info.metaDescription: What Cauce is, who it is for, what the Matamoros pilot includes and what comes next.
info.title: From the storm drain to the satellite.
info.lede: Cauce is a web app where residents of Matamoros report what floods their street with one photo. Together with water-level sensors, the rain forecast and satellite terrain data, it helps the authorities decide which drains to clear before the next storm.
info.context: Pilot in Matamoros, Tamaulipas. Project for the Mexican Space Agency (AEM) Hackathon.

diagram.alt: Cross-section of a street in Matamoros: a satellite observes the terrain and the rain, a resident reports a blocked storm drain, a sensor inside the drain measures the rising water, and the water flows through a pipe to the canal.

why.title: Why Matamoros
why.body: The city is almost flat: in the pilot area the ground sits between 3 and 21 meters above sea level, and the drainage saturates with every heavy storm. Many floods start with something small, like trash blocking a storm drain that nobody reported in time.

drain2022.body: The 20 de Noviembre canal overflows, mainly because of trash thrown into streets and canals.

storm2024.body: A storm affects 155 neighborhoods, according to the water and drainage board.

francine2024.body: Hurricane Francine floods streets across the city.

storm2025.body: A cloudburst floods hundreds of neighborhoods in Reynosa and Matamoros.

front2026.body: Cold front No. 1 drops 215.9 mm of rain. Buenavista, San Francisco, Los Sauces and Paseo Residencial are cut off.

residents.name: Residents
residents.body: They report from their phone in under 30 seconds, without an account, and confirm whether a problem is still there or has been fixed.

operators.name: Sensor operators
operators.body: They install water-level sensors in storm drains and canals, and check their status, alerts and history in their own portal.

authorities.name: Authorities
authorities.body: The water and drainage board and Civil Protection see the risk by area, why it is high and which drains to clear first.

scope.title: Pilot scope
scope.intro: What this version already does and what it leaves out, so nobody expects Cauce to be something it is not yet.

reports.title: One-photo reports
reports.body: Six problem types and automatic location. Without signal, the report is saved and sent once the connection is back.

signals.title: Resident confirmations
signals.body: “Still there” and “Fixed” keep the map up to date. Water reports expire after 24 hours unless someone confirms them.

sensors.title: Water-level sensors
sensors.body: Each sensor has its own warning and critical limits, and its status shows on the map.

panel.title: Risk panel
panel.body: Rain forecast, risk by area with its reasons, a list of drains to clear and report moderation.

operators.title: Operator portal
operators.body: Health of every sensor, alert history, configuration changes and CSV export.

ai.title: Category suggestion
ai.body: When enabled, an AI proposes the problem type from the photo. The resident decides.

pwa.title: Works on any phone
pwa.body: It opens in the browser and can be installed, without an app store.

alerts.title: Not an official warning system
alerts.body: It does not replace Civil Protection alerts. In an emergency, call 911.

prediction.title: No street-by-street flood prediction
prediction.body: Risk is a priority by area, in hexagons under 1 km², to decide where to act first.

hardware.title: No sensors installed yet
hardware.body: The readings in this demo come from a simulator that sends the same data as a real sensor.

accounts.title: No accounts or alerts for residents
accounts.body: Reporting is anonymous. Neighborhood alerts come in a later stage.

area.title: Matamoros only
area.body: Reports outside the pilot area are rejected.

demo.title: Includes demo data
demo.body: The map includes simulated reports and sensors based on real floods, labeled as such.

risk.title: How risk is calculated
risk.body: Each area gets a score from 0 to 100. It is a sum of five factors with fixed weights, and the panel always shows the reason and the number behind each one.
risk.caption: Weight of each factor in the score
risk.baseline: When the forecast brings no rain, the score shows as “baseline risk”: a preventive priority, not the absence of problems.

space.title: Space data
space.body: The terrain factor uses the Copernicus DEM GLO-90 elevation model from the European Space Agency, with 90-meter cells. In such a flat city, a few meters of difference decide where the water runs.

imerg.name: NASA GPM IMERG
imerg.body: Satellite-observed rainfall, to compare with what was forecast.

sentinel.name: Copernicus Sentinel-1
sentinel.body: Radar images that show where water remained after a storm, even under clouds.

inegi.name: INEGI CEM 15 m
inegi.body: More detailed elevation of Mexican territory to refine the terrain factor.

smap.name: NASA SMAP
smap.body: Soil moisture: saturated ground absorbs less rain.

items.pilot: Install the first sensors in Buenavista, San Francisco and Los Sauces, the neighborhoods that flood the most.
items.alerts: Alert the water board and Civil Protection by email or WhatsApp when a sensor reaches a critical level.
items.push: Alerts for residents about what is happening in their neighborhood.
items.accounts: Accounts and permissions for each agency, instead of the panel's shared password.
items.openData: Export reports and risk so other agencies can use them.

built.title: How it is built
built.body: Cauce is a progressive web app: it opens in the browser, can be installed and keeps reports even without signal. It asks for no personal data and strips photo metadata before uploading.
built.stack: Next.js and React, MapLibre maps with OpenFreeMap and OpenStreetMap, a Turso database, photos on Cloudflare R2, H3 hexagons and forecasts from Open-Meteo and Mexico's National Weather Service.
